edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. I, 4

source_text: Unguentum effusum nomen tuum. Propheticum sacramentum est. Tantummodo nomen Iesu venit in mundum et unguentum praedicatur effusum. Quomodo unguentum ad effusionem suam odorem longe lateque dispergit, sic Christi nomen, ubi nominatum fuerit, ubique suavitatem spargit. Multi habuerunt aromata. Regina Austri detulit aromata Solomoni et plures alii aromata possederunt, sed habuerit quis quantalibet, non possunt Christi odoribus comparari, de quo nunc sponsa ait: Odor unguentorum tuorum super omnia aromata. Ego arbitror quia et Moyses habuerit aromata et Aaron et singuli prophetarum; verum, si videro Christum et suavitatem unguentorum eius odore percepero, statim sententiam fero dicens: Odor unguentorum tuorum super omnia aromata.
pass_a_gloss: Ointment poured-out name yours. Prophetic sacrament it-is. Only name of-Jesus came into world and ointment is-preached poured-out. As ointment at its pouring scatters smell far-and-wide, so Christ's name wherever named spreads sweetness. Many had aromatics — Queen of-South brought aromatics to Solomon — but cannot compare to Christ's smells. Moses/Aaron/prophets had aromatics; if I-see Christ and perceive sweetness of his ointments, at-once I-judge: Smell of-ointments yours above all aromatics.
notes: Pass A literalist gloss ≠ Pass B literary English.
Song lemma sense-checked against Baehrens; Lawson ACW not used for wording.
pass_b_english: [[Your name is ointment poured out >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:3]]. It is a prophetic mystery. No sooner has the name of Jesus come into the world than ointment is proclaimed poured out. As ointment, when it is poured, spreads its fragrance far and wide, so Christ’s name, wherever it is named, scatters sweetness everywhere. Many have had spices. The queen of the South brought spices to Solomon, and many others have possessed spices; yet however many anyone may have had, they cannot be compared with Christ’s fragrances, of which the Bride now says: [[The fragrance of your ointments is above all spices >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:3]]. I judge that Moses too had spices, and Aaron, and each of the prophets; but if I see Christ and catch by smell the sweetness of his ointments, at once I give sentence and say: The fragrance of your ointments is above all spices.
